# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Decompose the `downtime-worker.ts` god class

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (8,105 lines, 174 exported symbols, 23 logical sections)

## Problem statement

`downtime-worker.ts` has grown into a single 8,105-line module that carries the
entire downtime-dispatch subsystem: constants, public types, idle detection,
the local-status poller, dispatchability gates, the Herdr list-head dispatch
pipeline, leader-election coordination, pane spawning and lifecycle, the worker
tick orchestrator, wl-output parsers, per-tier selection, settings clamps and
round-robin helpers. Navigating, reviewing and safely changing any one concern
requires holding the whole file in view, so every dispatch change carries
avoidable regression risk.

## Users

- **Downtime-dispatch maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one
  concern (e.g. a gate, a tier parser, the spawn path) without reasoning about
  8,000 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need to review a focused diff where the blast radius of
  a change is legible from the touched module.
- **Future agents implementing dispatch work items** need small, named modules
  they can locate with a file search instead of reading a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent implementing a dispatch-gate change, I want the gate logic in a
  dedicated module so that I can modify it without re-reading the whole worker.
- As a reviewer, I want a split diff to be attributable to a single concern so
  that I can verify it against its own tests.
- As a maintainer, I want each module under 1,000 lines so that the file is
  readable in a single pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (now a thin barrel) and for every
   module created by the split.
2. **Public surface preserved — used symbols only.** Every symbol currently
   imported from `./downtime-worker.js` by another module remains exported from
   that exact path with identical types and values, so the 33 importing files
   compile with no import-path edits. The barrel re-exports **only symbols that
   are actually used** by consumers; symbols that nothing outside the split
   modules imports are internal and need not be re-exported (producer decision
   on Q2).
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change;
   no test file is modified (not its import paths, fixtures or assertions), and
   all 15 `downtime-worker.*` test suites plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite
   pass unchanged.
4. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `downtime-worker.js` barrel; the dependency
   check reports no new cycles and does not extend the pre-existing
   `stalled-work ↔ downtime-worker` type-only cycle into runtime values.
5. **Single-flight state remains singular.** The module-level mutable
   `dispatchInFlightCount` (current line 2523) lives in exactly one module and
   is not duplicated by the split, so per-process dispatch single-flight
   semantics are unchanged.
6. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and the existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and update imports; do not refactor logic,
  rename public symbols, or change behaviour.
- **Barrel compatibility.** 33 files import from `./downtime-worker.js`,
  including 15 `downtime-worker.*` test suites (~15,000 test lines) and the
  production consumers `index.ts`, `settings.ts`, `ship-guard.ts`,
  `fetcher.ts`, `stalled-work.ts`, `worklist.ts`, plus 11 other test files.
  The barrel preserves that contract.
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf modules first (constants,
  types, clamps/parsers) and work inwards, so each merged step leaves the build
  and the full suite green.
- **No new runtime dependencies**, no test-file rewrites, no changes to the wl
  CLI contract or dispatch behaviour.
- **Scope boundary.** The item targets `downtime-worker.ts`; the other
  `packages/herdr` files above 1,000 lines are explicitly out of scope (see
  Risks — scope creep).

## Existing state

`downtime-worker.ts` is 8,105 lines. Its section inventory (line ranges from the
current `dev` checkout) is:

| # | Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---------|-------|------|
| 1 | Constants | 204–616 | 413 |
| 2 | Types | 617–709 | 93 |

| 7 | Dispatch (types + claim/result helpers) | 1249–2538 | 1,290 |
| 8 | Review-queue depth gate | 2539–2724 | 186 |
| 9 | Critical-only dispatch-window escape hatch | 2725–2776 | 52 |

| 11 | Leader-election coordination dispatch | 3696–5614 | 1,919 |
| 12 | Pane-lifecycle monitor | 5615–5773 | 159 |

| 17 | Audit-tier selection | 7148–7307 | 160 |
| 18 | Implement-tier selection | 7308–7471 | 164 |
| 19 | Plan/intake selection | 7472–7510 | 39 |

| 21 | Dependency frontier resolution | 7805–7913 | 109 |

| 23 | Round-robin helpers | 8035–8105 | 71 |

Relevant structural facts discovered during intake:

- **Module-level mutable state:** `let dispatchInFlightCount = 0` (line 2523)

- **Pre-existing coupling:** `stalled-work.ts` imports
  `parseDepListBlockersOutput`, `isAttemptBudgetExhausted`, `paneLabelItemId`
  and several types from `./downtime-worker.js`, while `downtime-worker.ts`
  imports `StalledPaneCandidate`, `StalledResumeOutcome` and `StalledScanOptions`
  types from `./stalled-work.js` — an existing type-only cycle that the split
  must not turn into a runtime cycle.
- **Precedent:** [WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO](../../../../.worklog) decomposed the
  2,584-line `src/database.ts` god class under ACs requiring an unchanged public
  API, tests passing without modification, and ≤500 lines per new module.

## Desired change

Reduce `downtime-worker.ts` to a thin re-export barrel and move its contents
into cohesive sibling modules, each well under 1,000 lines. A starting
decomposition (boundaries are an implementation decision, subject to the
constraints above):

| New module | Responsibility | Approx. size |
|---|---|---|
| `downtime-worker.constants.ts` | Tuning constants, floors/maxima, `decisionHeaderToken` | ~420 |
| `downtime-worker.types.ts` | Exported interfaces and unions (`LlamaStatus`, candidates, claim/result types, config, worker) | ~700 |
| `downtime-worker.idle.ts` | Idle detection, idle-duration tracker, per-slot tracker | ~255 |
| `downtime-worker.poller.ts` | `parseLlamaStatus`, `fetchLocalStatus`, `createDowntimePoller` | ~284 |
| `downtime-worker.gates.ts` | Soft-delete/assignee holds, review-queue depth gate, audit batch status, `classifyItemForDispatch`, attempt budget, critical-only escape hatch | ~480 |
| `downtime-worker.selection.ts` | wl-output parsers, per-tier selection, rotation, critical-first, dependency frontier | ~830 |
| `downtime-worker.clamps.ts` | `clampDowntime*` settings normalisers | ~130 |
| `downtime-worker.pane.ts` | Pane args/spawn options/spawn, pane-lifecycle monitor | ~360 |
| `downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` | Herdr list-head filter pipeline (`dispatchDowntimeWork`), prompt/comment builders | ~700–1,000 |
| `downtime-worker.coordination.ts` | `computeMostImportantItem`, `dispatchFromCoordination`, `runCoordinationCheckIn`, leader-election glue | ~1,000–1,300 (likely split into offers/leader) |
| `downtime-worker.orchestrator.ts` | `createDowntimeWorker` tick loop | ~930 |
| `downtime-worker.ts` | Thin barrel re-exporting the full public surface | ~150–250 |

Where a candidate module would still exceed 1,000 lines (coordination, dispatch),
it is split further along an existing section boundary rather than left oversized.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — reduce to a re-export barrel; preserve every current export.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` — new; extracted constants and `decisionHeaderToken`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — new; extracted exported types/interfaces.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.ts` — new; idle detection and trackers.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.poller.ts` — new; status parsing, fetch and poller.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — new; dispatchability gates and classification.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — new; wl parsers and per-tier selection.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.clamps.ts` — new; settings clamp helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts` — new; pane spawn and lifecycle monitor.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` — new; list-head dispatch pipeline and prompt builders.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts` — new; offer computation and coordinator dispatch (may split).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.ts` — new; `createDowntimeWorker` tick loop.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`, `settings.ts`, `ship-guard.ts`, `fetcher.ts`, `stalled-work.ts`, `worklist.ts` — verify unchanged (the barrel must keep them compiling as-is).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` — must remain unmodified; they are the behaviour-preservation gate.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — add a short module-layout note pointing at the new files.

## Related work

- **WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO** — *Decompose WorklogDatabase god class (src/database.ts, 2,584 lines)* (completed). Direct precedent: same refactor shape, same AC pattern (public API unchanged, tests pass unmodified, per-module line ceiling).

> Note: this sweep covered **production** files. Test files over 1,000 lines

> lockstep with their owning module during intake rather than filed as

### Tooling follow-up (cross-repo)

- **SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD** (SorraAgents) — *Refactor skill: detect files

- **Lost provenance / accidental logic drift (medium).** A large move invites

  and are **out of scope**; each is recorded as a linked follow-up rather than
  absorbed here.

**Q1 (scope)** — Is the "no file > 1000 lines" goal limited to
`downtime-worker.ts`, or should this item also split the other `packages/herdr`

# Canonical test suite excludes 76 root-level tests/*.test.ts files

## Problem Statement

`.pi/test-config.json` declares the canonical suite as `npm --silent test -- tests/cli` + `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`. Vitest therefore runs tests/cli (104 files) and tests/unit (43 files) only: the 76 root-level `tests/*.test.ts` files (`tests/read-cache.test.ts`, `tests/read-cache-cli.test.ts`, `tests/spawn-counter.test.ts`, `tests/audit.test.ts`, …) are never executed by /skill:test, implement.py finish, the pre-push hook, the ship release gate or an audit F3 auto-run.

## Goal

The canonical full suite executes every test file, or each exclusion is documented with a rationale.

## Users / Stakeholders

- **Agent tiers** (implement, audit, test): rely on the canonical full suite for gate enforcement.
- **Producer**: needs the canonical suite to be a reliable proxy for repo health.
- **CI**: uses `npm test` (full vitest suite, 370+ files) — the canonical subset is not a reliable proxy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The canonical suite command(s) in `.pi/test-config.json` cover root-level `tests/*.test.ts` files, or each exclusion is documented with a reason.
- A full /skill:test run reports the root-level files as executed (currently 0 of 76).
- Root-level failures surfaced by the change are triaged into test-failure items.
- Documented in docs/dev/ (test-suite layout) so work items cannot claim coverage the gate does not provide.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Runtime budget:** The existing canonical suite takes ~305s (tests/cli + tests/unit). The 76 root-level files add an unknown but potentially significant cost. Must be measured before/after.
- **Vitest configuration:** `vitest.config.ts` uses default glob patterns that discover all test files — the current suiteCommands narrow this to only `tests/cli` and `tests/unit`. Root-level files must be added without breaking the singleFork/isolation setup.
- **Overlapping basenames:** 4 files (`audit.test.ts`, `doctor-foreign-items-apply.test.ts`, `process-lifecycle.test.ts`, `sync-author-gate.test.ts`) exist at both root and in `tests/cli/` — these may be duplicates, relocations, or intentional variants. The change must not cause double-execution.
- **Related sibling:** WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 (canonical full suite excludes herdr package tests — completed) addresses the same root cause for a different scope; coordinate to avoid conflicting changes to `.pi/test-config.json`.

## Existing State

- `.pi/test-config.json`: declares `suiteCommands` as `tests/cli` + `tests/unit` (104 + 43 = 147 files)
- `vitest.config.ts`: discovers 370+ test files via default globs, but gates narrow to canonical subset
- 76 root-level `tests/*.test.ts` files never executed by any gate
- 4 files have both root and `tests/cli/` variants
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` documents canonical suite coverage but not the exclusion rationale

## Desired Change

Add the root-level test files to the canonical suite in `.pi/test-config.json` (either by expanding `suiteCommands` or introducing a named `groups` section — the test skill supports `groups` in the config), or document each exclusion with a rationale. Measure runtime impact. Update `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (or create `docs/dev/test-suite-layout.md`) with coverage documentation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/test-config.json` — add root-level test path to suiteCommands or groups
- `vitest.config.ts` — verify no conflicts with new glob patterns
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — update with new coverage numbers
- `tests/*.test.ts` — the 76 files to be covered (or documented as excluded)

# Decompose the `worklist.ts` god class

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — 7,823 lines, 89 exported symbols,
20 banner-delimited sections, one 2,260-line function (`runWorklistTui`, 5564–7823).

## Problem statement

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` carries the entire Herdr work-item selection
experience — constants and maps, the mutable list state machine, row/detail/meta
formatting, tooltip and help rendering, chord and key handling, the mouse input
pipeline, the list renderer, command dispatch and the TUI lifecycle loop — in a
single 7,823-line module. Because the biggest single concern (`runWorklistTui`,
2,260 lines of nested closures over one large mutable context) sits in the same
file as everything else, every change requires holding thousands of unrelated
lines in view, and the blast radius of a diff is not legible from the file it
touches.

This item is the follow-up filed by WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (producer directive,
intake Q1 → A: *"If any file is >1000 lines it should be evaluated for
refactoring and if appropriate a work item should be created"*). The
downtime-worker decomposition established the pattern this item reuses:
move-only extraction, thin compatibility barrel, tests untouched as the
behaviour gate, sequenced child items.

## Users

- **Herdr UI maintainers (agents and humans)** changing one concern (a key
  binding, the metadata panel, the mouse drag path, the refresh loop) without
  re-reading 7,800 lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** who need a diff whose blast radius is attributable to
  one module and one test file.
- **Future agents** implementing worklist work items, who need named modules
  locatable by file search instead of a monolith.
- **Operators** who benefit indirectly: smaller modules shorten the review and
  audit cycle for every worklist change.

Example user stories:

- As an agent changing the metadata panel, I want `formatMetadataPanel` and its
  helpers in their own module so that I can verify the change against its own
  tests.
- As a reviewer, I want the key-handling diff to touch only the key-handling
  module so that I can reason about input regressions in isolation.
- As a maintainer, I want every module under 1,000 lines so that any one concern
  is readable in a single pass.
- As a maintainer, I want `runWorklistTui` to be a thin orchestrator over named
  handler modules so that the TUI lifecycle is reviewable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No production file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports
   ≤1,000 for `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (reduced to a thin barrel) and for
   every module created by the split. The single 2,260-line `runWorklistTui`
   function is broken up so no module and no single exported function carries it
   whole.
2. **Public surface preserved — used symbols only.** Every symbol currently
   imported from `./worklist.js` by another module remains exported from that
   exact path with identical types and values, so the 34 importing files
   (2 production consumers + 32 test files, of which 22 are `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites) compile with no import-path edits. 66 distinct symbols are imported
   today; the barrel
   re-exports **only symbols consumers actually use** — unused exports stay
   internal to the extracted modules (inherited producer decision, parent
   WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 intake Q2 → "A, but only re-export symbols that are
   actually used").
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change,
   no renames of public symbols, no behavioural diffs. No test file is modified —
   not its import paths, fixtures or assertions — and all 22 `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites (15,433 lines) plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite pass unchanged.
4. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `worklist.js` barrel or from `index.ts`; the
   existing `worklist → fetcher/visibility/…` edge direction is preserved and no
   new cycle is introduced.
5. **State ownership is explicit and singular.** The mutable
   `WorkItemListState` (848-line section) and the TUI-local mutable context
   currently closed over by `runWorklistTui` each live in exactly one module;
   extraction must not duplicate mutable state or fork the source of truth.
6. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners such as
   `// ── Mouse / touch input (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ) ──`) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
7. **Testing/validation criterion:** the extracted modules are covered by the
   existing, unmodified `worklist*.test.ts` suites; the split adds no behaviour
   of its own, so no new assertions are required. Validation includes
   `tsc --noEmit`/build success, no new circular-import report, and a line-count
   check asserting every `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` production module is
   ≤1,000 lines.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and rewire imports; do not refactor logic,
  improve naming, or "fix" anything encountered on the way (record such findings
  as new work items instead).
- **Barrel compatibility.** 34 files import from `./worklist.js` or
  `./worklist` (including 22 `worklist*.test.ts` suites and the production
  consumers `index.ts` and `fetcher.ts`). The barrel preserves that contract.
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf modules first (constants,
  types, layout, formatting) and work inwards towards the state machine and the
  TUI loop, so each merged step leaves the build and the full suite green.
- **`runWorklistTui` is the hard part.** Its 2,260 lines are nested closures
  sharing one large mutable context. The extraction must keep a single context
  object (interface-typed, owned by one module) and pass it explicitly to
  extracted handler functions rather than duplicating state or converting to a
  class-based controller (that would be a behavioural rewrite, not a move).
- **No new runtime dependencies**, no test-file rewrites, no changes to Herdr
  key bindings, shortcuts, rendering output or the `wl` CLI contract.
- **Scope boundary.** This epic targets production modules under
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts`. Test files exceeding the ceiling
  (`worklist.test.ts` 7,073 lines, `worklist-mouse.test.ts` 1,132 lines) are
  **out of scope** under the recommended option (see Appendix Q1) and would be
  filed as a follow-up item, because splitting them would violate AC3
  (unmodified tests as the behaviour gate).
- **Other >1,000-line herdr files are out of scope** (tracked separately:
  `index.ts` WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6, `fetcher.ts` WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1,
  `dispatcher-anchor.ts` WL-0MVGKHCP9005SJPZ, `downtime-log.ts`
  WL-0MVGKHFT4003X6JW, `downtime-worker.ts` WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7).

## Existing state

ranges from the current `dev` checkout):

  pane markers and event subscriptions (5606–6141), metadata blocker resolution

  `command-log`, `form-dialog`, `clipboard`, `ship-it-dialog`, `key-input`,
  `grouping`, `md-viewer`, `md-note-edit` and `@worklog/shared/icons`. Nothing
  outside imports the individual UI internals, so the extracted modules have a
  clean one-way boundary to preserve.
- **Precedent:** WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (downtime-worker.ts, 8,105 → thin barrel,
  sequenced child items) and WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO (`src/database.ts`, 2,584
  lines, completed) used the same AC shape: unchanged public API, tests pass
  unmodified, per-module line ceiling.

## Desired change

Reduce `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` to a thin re-export barrel and move its

## Decompose the `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` god module

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (2,798 lines, 37 exported symbols)

## Problem statement

`packages/herdr/src/index.ts` is the Herdr plugin entry point and has grown to
2,798 lines. It currently carries command routing, argument builders, background
dispatch, pane-ID capture, claim/priority resolution, interactive window and tab
placement, pane cleanup, dozens of production dependency resolvers, the
downtime-worker dependency factory, settings bootstrap and the full TUI
`main()` loop in one module. Navigating, reviewing and safely changing any one
concern requires holding the whole file in view, so every dispatch or TUI change
carries avoidable regression risk.

The 1,000-line maintainability ceiling was adopted for the parent refactor
series WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7. This item is the `index.ts` member of that sweep and
was created specifically to bring this file under the ceiling.

## Users

- **Herdr plugin maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one concern
  (e.g. background dispatch, interactive placement, the TUI loop) without
  reasoning about 2,800 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need a focused diff whose blast radius is legible from
  the touched module.
- **Future agents implementing plugin work items** need small, named modules
  they can locate with a file search instead of reading a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent implementing a background-dispatch change, I want that path in a
  dedicated module so I can modify it without re-reading the TUI loop.
- As a reviewer, I want a split diff attributable to a single concern so I can
  verify it against its own tests.
- As a maintainer, I want each module under 1,000 lines so a file is readable in
  a single pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000
   for `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (now a thin barrel/entry module) and for
   every module created by the split.
2. **Public surface preserved — used symbols only.** Every symbol currently
   imported from `./index.js` by another module remains exported from that exact
   path with identical types and values, so `index.test.ts`, `claim.test.ts`,
   `fetchAuditItemById.test.ts` and `start.ts` compile with no import-path edits.
   The barrel re-exports **only symbols that are actually used** by consumers;
   unused exports stay internal to the extracted modules (inherited producer
   decision Q2 on the parent item, WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7).
3. **Entry-point behaviour preserved.** `start.ts` dynamically imports
   `./index.js` and calls `main()`; `index.ts` keeps exporting `main` and keeps
   the `isEntryPoint` guard so importing the module in a vitest worker still does
   not launch the TUI or call `process.exit`. The entry guard stays in the entry
   module (not in an extracted helper) so `process.argv[1]` identity checks keep
   their current meaning.
4. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change;
   no test file is modified (not its import paths, fixtures or assertions), and
   all `packages/herdr` test suites pass unchanged.
5. **Module-level singletons stay singular.** The `const settings =
   loadSettings()` side effect (currently line 2246) is evaluated **exactly once**
   at module load and shared by `createDowntimeDeps` and `main()`. It must not be
   duplicated into two modules, or the plugin would load settings twice with
   potentially different results. The same rule applies to the resolved script
   paths (`SEND_TO_PI_SCRIPT`, `RUN_IN_PANE_SCRIPT`) which depend on
   `import.meta.url` staying in `packages/herdr/src/`.
6. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `index.js` barrel; the barrel imports downward
   only. The dependency check reports no new cycles (including the existing
   `stalled-work ↔ downtime-worker` type-only cycle, which must not be widened).
7. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, and `npm run build`
   (tsc) must succeed — a module move that breaks the build is not a valid
   intermediate state.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and update imports; do not refactor logic, rename
  public symbols, or change behaviour.
- **Barrel compatibility.** 3 test files and `start.ts` import from
  `./index.js`; the barrel preserves that contract (AC2/AC3).
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf modules first and work inwards,
  so each merged step leaves the build and the full suite green.
- **No new runtime dependencies**, no test-file rewrites, no changes to the wl
  CLI contract or to plugin behaviour.
- **Scope boundary.** This item targets `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` only. Test
  file size (`index.test.ts` is 3,977 lines), sibling production files and a
  repo-wide lint rule are out of scope (see Risks — scope creep).

## Existing state

`index.ts` is 2,798 lines. Its cohesive sections (line ranges from the current
`dev` checkout) are:

| # | Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---------|-------|------|
| 1 | Header, imports and resolved script paths | 1–174 | 174 |
| 2 | Command routing + arg builders (`routeCommand`, `stripCommandPrefix`, `buildSendToPiArgs`, `buildRunInPaneArgs`, `parsePaneIdFile`) | 176–376 | 201 |
| 3 | Background (no-pane) dispatch (`BACKGROUND_LOG_DIR`, log helpers, `spawnBackgroundShell`, `spawnBackgroundPi`) | 377–579 | 203 |
| 4 | Pane-ID capture + work-item extraction (`CAPTURE_*`, `capturePaneIdFromFile`, `extractWorkItemId`) | 580–675 | 96 |
| 5 | Claim + interactive priority (`claimItemForAgentCommand`, `resolveInteractiveDispatchPriority`, priority lookup, critical blockers) | 676–794 | 119 |
| 6 | Default anchor resolvers (dispatcher/project/tab/item, internal) | 795–895 | 101 |
| 7 | Interactive placement + root-pane cleanup (`resolveInteractiveWorkspaceId`, `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor`, `closeInteractiveTabRootPane`, `defaultInteractiveLiveTrackedPanesResolver`, `defaultInteractiveClosePane`) | 896–1111 | 216 |
| 8 | Downtime/stalled resolvers (`defaultRunningDowntimePanesResolver`, `defaultStalledResume*`, `defaultStalledPanesLister`, `worklogRootFromPiSessionPath`, `defaultStalledPaneRootResolver`, `readClosedPaneIds`) | 1112–1319 | 208 |
| 9 | `createDowntimeDeps` dependency factory | 1323–2244 | 922 |
| 10 | Settings bootstrap (`const settings = loadSettings()`) | 2246 | 1 |
| 11 | Worklog target configuration (`configureWorklogTarget`, `uninitializedReport`) | 2261–2283 | 23 |
| 12 | TUI `main()` loop | 2284–2783 | 500 |
| 13 | Entry-point guard (`isEntryPoint` + `main().catch`) | 2785–2798 | 14 |

Relevant structural facts discovered during intake:

- **Used public surface (26 symbols):** static imports from `./index.js` are
  `stripCommandPrefix`, `routeCommand`, `stripAgentPromptPrefix`,
  `buildSendToPiArgs`, `buildRunInPaneArgs`, `createDowntimeDeps`,
  `capturePaneIdFromFile`, `parsePaneIdFile`, `buildBackgroundLogPath`,
  `spawnBackgroundShell`, `spawnBackgroundPi`, `formatBackgroundFailure`,
  `CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `extractWorkItemId`, `defaultStalledPaneRootResolver`,
  `defaultStalledPanesLister`, `worklogRootFromPiSessionPath`,
  `resolveInteractiveDispatchPriority`, `claimItemForAgentCommand`; dynamic
  `import('./index.js')` in `index.test.ts` additionally uses
  `configureWorklogTarget`, `uninitializedReport`,
  `defaultInteractiveLiveTrackedPanesResolver`, `resolveInteractiveWorkspaceId`,
  `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor`, `closeInteractiveTabRootPane`; `start.ts`
  dynamically uses `main`.
- **Unused exported symbols (safe to keep internal):** `CommandRoute`,
  `BACKGROUND_LOG_DIR`, `BackgroundSpawnDeps`, `CAPTURE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`,
  `PaneIdFileDeps`, `InteractiveLiveTrackedPanesResult`,
  `InteractiveRootPaneCleanupDeps`, `defaultInteractiveClosePane`,
  `defaultRunningDowntimePanesResolver`, `defaultStalledResumePromptAgent`,
  `defaultStalledResumeStartAgent`.
- **Single module-level side effect:** `const settings = loadSettings()` at line
  2246, read by `createDowntimeDeps` (line 2144) and `main()`. No other top-level
  statements exist beyond the entry guard.
- **Entry point chain:** `herdr-plugin.toml` launches
  `npx tsx src/start.ts`; `start.ts` dynamically imports `./index.js` and calls
  `main()`. The `isEntryPoint` guard in both modules prevents test-time launch.
- **Test gate:** `index.test.ts` (3,977 lines), `claim.test.ts` (407), and
  `fetchAuditItemById.test.ts` (281) import the module and must stay unmodified.
- **Precedent:** WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO decomposed the 2,584-line
  `src/database.ts` god class under ACs requiring an unchanged public API,
  tests passing without modification, and per-module line ceilings.
- **Parent decisions inherited:** scope limited to this file with follow-up items
  for the rest (Q1 → A); keep a public barrel re-exporting used symbols only
  (Q2 → A refined); delivery as an epic decomposed into sequenced child items,
  leaf-first (Q3 → A). See WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 Appendix.

## Desired change

Reduce `index.ts` to a thin re-export barrel plus the entry-point guard and
shared bootstrap side effect, and move its contents into cohesive sibling
modules. A starting decomposition (boundaries are an implementation decision,
subject to the constraints above):

| New module | Responsibility | Approx. size |
|---|---|---|
| `index.commands.ts` | `routeCommand`, `stripCommandPrefix`, `buildSendToPiArgs`, `buildRunInPaneArgs`, `parsePaneIdFile` and command-prefix helpers | ~210 |
| `index.background.ts` | Background (no-pane) dispatch: log paths, failure formatting, `spawnBackgroundShell`, `spawnBackgroundPi` | ~205 |
| `index.pane-capture.ts` | `capturePaneIdFromFile`, capture constants, `extractWorkItemId` | ~100 |
| `index.claim.ts` | `claimItemForAgentCommand`, interactive dispatch priority and critical-blocker lookup | ~120 |
| `index.interactive.ts` | Interactive workspace/item anchor resolution, tab root-pane cleanup and live-tracked-pane resolvers | ~220 |
| `index.resolvers.ts` | Production default resolvers for dispatcher/project/item anchors, running downtime panes, stalled panes and worklog root | ~310 |
| `index.downtime-deps.ts` | `createDowntimeDeps` and its internal helpers (includes the `fetchAuditItemById` closure) | ~925 |
| `index.settings.ts` | Single `settings = loadSettings()` instance and `configureWorklogTarget`/`uninitializedReport` bootstrap helpers | ~30 |
| `index.main.ts` | The TUI `main()` loop | ~505 |
| `index.ts` | Thin barrel re-exporting used symbols + entry-point guard | ~120–200 |

If any candidate module still exceeds the ceiling, it is split further along the
section boundary rather than left oversized. `createDowntimeDeps` is the largest
single unit (922 lines) and may need its `fetchAuditItemById` closure extracted to
stay clearly under the limit.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — reduce to a thin barrel + entry-point guard; preserve every used export.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.commands.ts` — new; command routing and argument builders.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.background.ts` — new; background dispatch and log handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.pane-capture.ts` — new; pane-ID capture and work-item extraction.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.claim.ts` — new; claim and interactive priority.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.interactive.ts` — new; interactive placement and pane cleanup.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.resolvers.ts` — new; default dependency resolvers.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.downtime-deps.ts` — new; `createDowntimeDeps` factory.

- `packages/herdr/src/start.ts`, `index.test.ts`, `claim.test.ts`, `fetchAuditItemById.test.ts` — must remain unmodified; they are the behaviour-preservation gate.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — module-layout note pointing at the new files.
- `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md` — update the `index.ts` production-wiring reference if paths move.
- `docs/dev/rca-downtime-3-consecutive-wl-cli-errors.md` — update the `createDowntimeDeps` file reference if it moves.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7** — *downtime-worker.ts is a god class* (parent refactor series; discovered-from). Source of the 1,000-line sweep and the producer's Q1–Q3 decisions.
- **WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO** — *Decompose WorklogDatabase god class (src/database.ts, 2,584 lines)* (completed). Direct precedent: same refactor shape, same AC pattern.

- **WL-0MT2GITCX009WUEW** — *Remove packages/herdr/src/icons.ts and rewire herdr consumers* (completed). Related herdr consumer-rewiring precedent.

- `docs/dev/rca-downtime-3-consecutive-wl-cli-errors.md` — references `createDowntimeDeps` in `index.ts`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MT2GITCX009WUEW** – Remove packages/herdr/src/icons.ts and rewire herdr consumers (completed)
- **WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4** – herdr plugin crashes at startup: Cannot find package 'marked' (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND) (completed)

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

## Risks and assumptions

- **Barrel-induced runtime cycle (medium).** A module that imports from
  `index.js` would create a cycle through the barrel. *Mitigation:* extracted
  modules import only concrete siblings; the barrel imports downward only
  (AC6).
- **Duplicate settings load (medium).** `const settings = loadSettings()` must
  live in exactly one module. *Mitigation:* AC5; keep it in a leaf
  `index.settings.ts` consumed by both `createDowntimeDeps` and `main()`.
- **Broken entry point (high).** `start.ts` imports `main()` and the
  `isEntryPoint` guard depends on `process.argv[1]`. *Mitigation:* AC3 keeps
  `main` and the guard in `index.ts`; the plugin-startup tests and
  `vitest run` on `index.test.ts` are the gate.
- **Lost provenance / accidental logic drift (medium).** A large move invites
  silent edits. *Mitigation:* move-only rule, unchanged test suite (AC4), and a

- **Test-file temptation (low).** Updating `index.test.ts` import paths is the
  easy path but erases the behaviour-preservation signal. *Mitigation:* AC2/AC4

## Assumptions

- Each sequenced child lands tree-green: `npm run build` succeeds and the full
  suite passes before the next child starts.
- The decomposition will be delivered as an epic with sequenced child items (one
  per extracted module), landed leaf-first and independently green (parent Q3).

# Refactor: decompose `packages/shared/src/database.ts` god class

## Problem statement

`packages/shared/src/database.ts` is 3,684 lines and holds a single
`WorklogDatabase` class with 109 methods spanning at least ten unrelated
concerns (work-item CRUD, hierarchy traversal, dependency-edge reconciliation,
comment storage, audit results, FTS/semantic search, sort-index management, the
`wl next` selection pipeline, JSONL import/export, and Git/JSONL sync). It
breaches the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 and is hard to navigate, review, and change safely.

## Users

- **Agents implementing work items** — need to locate the code for one concern
  without reading 3,684 lines; large files inflate context cost and increase
  the chance of editing the wrong overload.
- **Reviewers / producers auditing changes** — need diffs scoped to one
  responsibility; a 3,684-line file makes review of a 20-line behavioural
  change impractical.
- **Operators debugging `wl next`** — need the selection pipeline (the largest
  cluster: ~1,150 lines) to be readable in isolation.

Example user stories:

- As an agent, I want `wl next` selection logic in its own module, so that a
  change to selection ordering does not require loading CRUD, sync and comment
  code into context.
- As a reviewer, I want each extracted module to have a single stated
  responsibility, so that I can judge a diff against one boundary.
- As a maintainer, I want the public `WorklogDatabase` API unchanged, so that
  no CLI/Herdr/TUI consumer needs touching.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ceiling met.** `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and every file under
   `packages/shared/src/database/` is ≤ 1,000 lines (target: largest extracted
   module ≤ 700). Verified with `wc -l` output recorded in the work item.
2. **Public API unchanged.** `WorklogDatabase` (all public method signatures and
   constructor), plus `WorklogDatabaseServices`, `JsonlImportResult`,
   `GitTarget`, `UpdateIfMatchesResult` and `normalizeTitleForMatch` remain
   importable from the unchanged specifier `@worklog/shared` (entry
   `dist/database.js`). No changes to `src/**` or `packages/herdr/src/**`
   consumer code.
3. **Move-only, behaviour-preserving.** No logic, SQL, error-message, ordering,
   or schema changes; existing test assertions are unmodified and the suite is
   green. Test files may be split/moved only where a test file itself exceeds
   1,000 lines (lockstep rule), with import paths the only mechanical change.
4. **No circular imports.** The extracted-module import graph is acyclic; no
   module imports the `database.ts` façade. Shared types live in a context
   module that every extracted module may import.
5. **Responsibilities documented.** `packages/shared/README.md` (Package
   Structure) and each new module's header comment state its single
   responsibility and its boundary.
6. **No performance regression** in the `wl next` path: `npm run
   benchmark:wl-next:json` pre/post comparison within run-to-run noise (the
   extraction moves code only, and `EdgeCache`/effective-priority caching
   semantics are unchanged).
7. **Builds and tests.** `npm run build:shared`, `npm run build` and the full
   project test suite all pass.
8. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes,
   including code comments, `packages/shared/README.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`,
   `docs/dev/fts.md`, `docs/dependency-reconciliation.md` and
   `docs/design/incremental-sync.md` (each currently names
   `packages/shared/src/database.ts` as the home of a concern).

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Extraction and method relocation only; no "while we're here"
  rewrites. Method-level decomposition of the two oversized methods
  (`handleCriticalEscalation`, 324 lines; `findNextWorkItemFromItems`, 251
  lines) is allowed **only** where required to keep an extracted file under the
  ceiling, and must land as a separate commit from the pure move.
- **No public-API growth.** Private hooks needed by extracted modules are
  expressed through an internal context type, not by making `WorklogDatabase`
  members public.
- **Icons import guard (WL-0MT2GMTAZ003VKVL).** `tests/unit/icons.test.ts`
  scans every `.ts`/`.js` file with `ICONS_FILE_RE` and fails on any relative
  `icons.js`/`icons.ts` import. Extracted modules must keep using
  `@worklog/shared/icons`.
- **`src/database.ts` (93-line CLI shim) is unchanged.**
- **No new runtime dependencies.**
- **Serialize with WL-0MVGKGJXJ000ISBU** (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`,
  2,225 lines) — same package and build; running both decompositions
  concurrently would churn `packages/shared/dist` and invite merge conflicts.
- **Escaped backticks** only in written content; Markdown otherwise.

## Existing state

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — 3,684 lines, 6 exports: the
  `WorklogDatabase` class (109 methods), `normalizeTitleForMatch`, and four
  interfaces (`JsonlImportResult`, `GitTarget`, `UpdateIfMatchesResult`,
  `WorklogDatabaseServices`).
- Entry point: `packages/shared/package.json` → `main`/`exports["."]` =
  `./dist/database.js`; `src/database.ts` (root, 93 lines) is a thin CLI
  shim wiring CLI-specific services and re-exporting the shared class.
- Consumers: ~54 files reference the class (`src/**`, `packages/herdr/src/**`,
  `tests/**`, `scripts/**`, `bench/**`), all via `@worklog/shared` or the
  shim — none import internal members.
- Tests in lockstep: `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` (834),
  `database-dedup.test.ts` (134), `dirty-tracking.test.ts` (384),
  `audit-fingerprint-repair.test.ts` (135) — all under 1,000; plus root
  `tests/database.test.ts` (3,651) and `tests/next-regression.test.ts`
  (2,112), which exceed the ceiling and are therefore in scope for
  lockstep splitting.
- **Prior attempt did not land.** WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO ("Decompose
  WorklogDatabase god class", completed) extracted `src/lib/edge-cache.ts` and
  `src/lib/audit-store.ts` on the feature branch only — neither file exists in
  the current tree, and the class has since grown from 2,584 to 3,684 lines.
  This item therefore restarts from a single-class module, and the regrowth is
  the reason the decomposition needs a clear ownership boundary rather than
  ad-hoc extraction.

## Desired change

| `database/work-items.ts` | Item CRUD (`create`, `createWithNextSortIndex`, `get`, `update`, `updateIfMatches`, `delete`, `list`, duplicate detection, diff helpers) | ~470 |
| `database/hierarchy.ts` | Children/descendants/depth/leaf queries, `cascadePriorityDowngrade`, `demoteParentOnChildAdded`, `revertToPlanComplete` | ~200 |
| `database/dependencies.ts` | Edge CRUD, `buildEdgeCache`, blocker queries, dependency-status reconciliation | ~260 |
| `database/comments.ts` | Comment CRUD, `upsertComments`/`importComments`, activity stamping | ~180 |
| `database/audit.ts` | Audit-result CRUD, waiver set/clear, invalidation reconcile, audit map + not-ready freshness | ~130 |
| `database/sort.ts` | `sortItemsByScore`, sort-index compute/assign/preview, `reSort`, `orderBySortIndex`, audit-tier comparison, `selectBySortIndex` | ~310 |
| `database/priority.ts` | `getPriorityValue`, `riskOrdinal`, `effortOrdinal`, `matchesRiskEffort`, `computeEffectivePriority` | ~200 |
| `database/next-pipeline.ts` | `findNextWorkItem`/`findNextWorkItems`/`findNextWorkItemFromItems`, `applyFilters`, `filterCandidates`, `resolveBlockerToRoot`, `selectHighestPriorityBlocking` | ~600 |
| `database/critical-escalation.ts` | `handleCriticalEscalation` and its private helpers (may require an internal split to stay under budget) | ~330 |
| `database/search.ts` | `search`, `rebuildFtsIndex`, semantic-index create/trigger/remove | ~210 |
| `database/sync.ts` | `refreshFromGit`, `exportForSync`, export timestamps, `countDirtyRecords`, delta metadata, `deleteLocalJsonl`, `refreshFromJsonlIfNewer`, auto-sync triggers | ~380 |

1. **Foundation** — create `database/` and `database/context.ts` (internal
   types, EdgeCache, children map, id generation, prefix accessors). Blocks the
   rest.
2. **`wl next` cluster** — `priority.ts`, `next-pipeline.ts`,
   `critical-escalation.ts` (largest win, highest risk).
3. **Ordering & audit** — `sort.ts`, `audit.ts`.
4. **Items & hierarchy** — `work-items.ts`, `hierarchy.ts`.
5. **Dependencies & comments** — `dependencies.ts`, `comments.ts`.

   evidence, build and full suite.

independently verifiable.

  stay byte-compatible at the type level

  `dirty-tracking.test.ts`, `audit-fingerprint-repair.test.ts` — imports stay
  `./database.js`; assertions unchanged

- `tests/next-regression.test.ts` (2,112) — split in lockstep, move-only

- **Behaviour drift in the `wl next` pipeline** (largest, most intricate
  cluster; 324- and 251-line methods). *Mitigation:* pure move first; split
  oversized methods in separate commits; `tests/next-regression.test.ts`
  and `docs/validation/status-stage-inventory.md` act as the behaviour oracle.
- **Circular imports** (`next-pipeline` ↔ `dependencies` ↔ `priority`).
  *Mitigation:* `context.ts` owns shared types; modules receive collaborators
  through the context; façade is never imported by a module.
- **Hidden `this.` coupling.** Several "private" helpers are shared across
  concerns (`buildEdgeCache`, `generateId`, `buildAuditMapForItems`,
  `compareTrackedFields`, `getPriorityValue`, `getNonClosedChildren`,
  `debug`). *Mitigation:* inventory every `this.` call per method before the
  move and express it on the context type.

  `dist/database.js`; the façade must keep that path and re-export every type.
- **Performance regression** through changed cache lifetimes. *Mitigation:*
  `npm run benchmark:wl-next:json` before and after the `wl next` cluster.

  decomposition). *Mitigation within scope:* documented module boundaries and
  single-responsibility headers. A repo-wide file-size guard is **out of
  scope** here and filed separately (see Related work) to avoid scope creep.

  test files only when they are touched in lockstep with their module.

  `scripts/` and `bench/`.

  observed en route becomes a separate `discovered-from` work item.

  `docs/dependency-reconciliation.md` (§ reconciliation logic),

  (`findNextWorkItemFromItems`).

  `discovered-from:WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT`).

## Appendix: decision log (agent-proposed; producer may override)

No producer interview questions were required: the seed context (goal, drafted
ACs, parent directive) is sufficient to draft an actionable brief, and every
remaining choice is a reversible design decision that the plan/implement stages
can adjust. The three decisions below were taken by the agent and are recorded
for review.

- **Q: How should extracted modules relate to `WorklogDatabase`?**
  **Recommended and chosen: (a)** pure functional modules operating on an
  injected internal context type, with `WorklogDatabase` as a delegating
  façade. Rationale: testable without a database, no inheritance/mixin
  complexity, and the import graph stays acyclic (the façade depends on the
  modules, never the reverse).
  Alternatives considered: (b) composed private helper classes instantiated by
  the façade (more state plumbing, harder to test in isolation); (c) mixins /
  `extends` chains (fragile, obscures the public surface).

- **Q: What child granularity?**
  **Recommended and chosen:** six children (foundation; `wl next` cluster;
  ordering & audit; items & hierarchy; dependencies & comments; search, sync &
  import/export + closeout). Rationale: each child is independently move-only,
  verifiable with the full suite, and small enough to review; the riskiest
  cluster (`wl next`) is isolated so a regression is bisectable.
  Alternatives considered: ~13 children (one per module — more overhead and
  churn than value); one child (no bisectable checkpoints).

- **Q: Add a file-size regression guard (CI/lint) in this item?**

  affecting every sibling god-class item, not a property of this file.
  Filed as a separate low-priority `chore` item (`discovered-from` this item).

- **Q: Should the oversized test files (`tests/database.test.ts` 3,651;
  `tests/next-regression.test.ts` 2,112) be split?**
  **Recommended and chosen: yes, mechanical split only**, in lockstep with the

# Remove dead top-level `singleFork` key in vitest.config.ts

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

`vitest.config.ts` sets `singleFork: true` at the top level of the `test`
block. Vitest 4 has no such top-level option — `singleFork` is a
`poolOptions.forks.*` key — so the setting is silently ignored (no warning is
emitted). The comment directly above it, "Force per-file isolation by limiting
to 1 active worker per file sequence", describes behaviour that is actually
provided by `isolate: true` + `maxWorkers: 4` (+ `pool: 'forks'`).

The dead key is harmless today, but it is misleading: a future reader may
believe the suite is serialised, and a migration to an option shape that *is*
read (or vitest version churn that starts warning) could confuse diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `singleFork: true` is removed from `vitest.config.ts`.
- The comment above it is rewritten (or removed) to state what actually
  enforces per-file isolation (`pool: 'forks'`, `isolate: true`,
  `maxWorkers: 4`), and that parallelism is otherwise intentional.
- Full canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) stays green with the same
  test counts; no runtime regression in either wall-clock or aggregate test
  time on the same host.

## Out of scope

Bumping `maxWorkers` / `fileParallelism` — that is the follow-up "Test-suite
parallelism: reconsider maxWorkers on hosts with more cores".

# Investigate in-process CLI harness cost (~200 ms per invocation)

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

Timing the in-process CLI harness (`tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts`,
`runInProcess()`, used by `execAsync` in `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts`):

- `--help` (no DB work): ~72 ms per invocation
- `list --json`, `create`, `status`: ~196–257 ms per invocation

The canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) makes roughly 1200 such
in-process invocations — about 240 s of aggregate test time across
`close-recursive` (46 tests), `issue-management` (49), `issue-status` (43),
`valid-json-output` (38) and `json-output-shape` (18), plus seeding in
`beforeEach` hooks.

Every invocation constructs a fresh `Command`, re-registers ~35 built-in
commands, loads config, opens a SQLite database (with schema/migrations) and
closes it. The suite measured 624 s → 427–547 s after WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8, and
this in-process pool is the next largest remaining aggregate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Profile one `runInProcess` call and attribute the per-call cost
  (commander registration vs config load vs DB open/close vs command action).
- Where the cost is test-harness overhead (not production behaviour being
  asserted), reduce it without changing what each test asserts — candidates:
  reusing the command/plugin-context across calls for stateless reads,
  avoiding repeated YAML config parses, sharing DB open across calls within a
  test file.
- If the cost is production CLI startup (DB schema/migrations, plugin scan),
  record the findings and re-scope: the change then belongs in `src/` and is a
  production decision, not a test-only change.
- Canonical suite stays green with unchanged test counts; median wall-clock
  on a consistent host improves versus the pre-change baseline of this item.

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

The canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) runs with `maxWorkers: 4`
in `vitest.config.ts` (pool `'forks'`, `isolate: true`). The dev host has 16
cores. WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 reduced per-spawn cost ~5× (bundle-based CLI
spawning) and cut the wall clock 30–35 % at matched load, but wall clock
remains dominated by the longest single files on the critical path
(`sync-vs-mutation` ~151 s, `close-recursive` ~121 s, `issue-management`
~88 s, `read-cache-spawn-reduction` ~84 s).

The brief explicitly listed parallelisation as out of scope ("record as
linked follow-up work items, not this brief") — hence this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Measure the canonical suite at `maxWorkers` 4 vs 6 vs 8 on a 16-core host
  (median of ≥3 runs per setting, load quoted per run; report aggregate test
  time as the load-independent metric).
- Confirm memory headroom: RSS per worker tracked; no OOM at the chosen
  setting (the config comment cites memory guardrails as the reason for 4).
- Confirm determinism: 3 consecutive green runs at the chosen setting, no
  intermittent test-timeout or hook-timeout failures.
- Decide and record: either adopt a higher `maxWorkers` (documented) or
  formally keep 4 with the measurement evidence.

# Maintenance routines skill: create/maintain daily scheduled test, standup, refactor sessions at high priority

## Headline

A new ContextHub skill (`/skill:maintenance-routines`) that creates and maintains the required daily scheduled maintenance sessions (test 07:00, standup 08:00, refactor 09:00) in each project's `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatching all of them at **high request priority** so they are processed even in peak periods — backed by a herdr enhancement that threads a per-entry `priority` (default `high`) into the `X-Priority` request header.

## Problem statement

Every project should run regular automated maintenance routines (test suite, standup report, refactor pass). The herdr plugin already has the mechanism (`scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatched on idle by the downtime worker), but there is no maintained, canonical set: the current template/live config only carries `/skill:refactor` (3-day interval, no time) and `/skill:standup` (06:05, no priority), and **no** `/skill:test` routine. Worse, dispatched scheduled prompts have no work item, so they receive the downtime request-priority default `medium` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority(undefined)` → `medium`) — they can be starved behind peak-period contention. The operator wants the three routines scheduled daily (07:00/08:00/09:00) and dispatched at **high** priority.

## Users

- **Project operator** — wants the three routines to reliably exist in each project's schedule and to be processed even in peak periods.
- **Automated maintenance sessions** (`/skill:test`, `/skill:standup`, `/skill:refactor`) — must carry `X-Priority: high` on every provider request so `llama-proxy` serves them ahead of the contention queue.

### Example user stories

- As an operator, I run `/skill:maintenance-routines` on a project and it ensures `/skill:test` (daily 07:00), `/skill:standup` (daily 08:00) and `/skill:refactor` (daily 09:00) are present and correctly configured in `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, without touching my last-run timestamps or any custom entries.
- As an operator, I know every scheduled maintenance session is dispatched with `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY=high` (→ `X-Priority: high`), so the daily test/standup/refactor runs are served even during peak periods.
- As an operator, when I provision a new project with `wl init`, it comes pre-loaded with the same three routines (daily, timed, high priority).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Skill exists and reconciles the schedule.** `skill/maintenance-routines/` ships a `SKILL.md`, a reconciler script and unit tests. Invoking it (or the script directly) reconciles the project-local `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (under the resolved worklog dir) so these required routines are present and exact:
   - `/skill:test` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "07:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:standup` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "08:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:refactor` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "09:00"`, `priority: "high"`
2. **Reconcile is non-destructive and idempotent.** Entries are created if absent; drifted fields (interval/time/priority) are corrected; `lastTriggeredAt` and all other user-defined entries are preserved verbatim; a second run makes no further changes; missing or malformed config files are handled fail-closed with a clear report; `--dry-run` shows the planned diff without writing.
3. **Herdr honours a per-entry `priority` field.** `ScheduledPrompt` gains an optional `priority` (`low|medium|high|critical`) validated in `parseScheduledPrompt` (invalid value → entry skipped with a warning, fail-closed); **absent → defaults to `high`** for scheduled prompts. The scheduled-prompt dispatch passes it through `spawnAgentPane({ priority })` → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` (so `high` → `X-Priority: high` on every request). Unit tests cover parse defaults/validation and the dispatch threading.
4. **Template provisions the required set.** `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the `wl init` base set) is updated to the three required routines with daily `intervalDays`, `time` and `priority: high`, so new projects are provisioned with the routines (create-if-absent semantics unchanged — existing configs are never clobbered).
5. **Documentation criterion.** `packages/herdr/README.md` (Scheduled prompts section), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (Request priority section) and `CONFIG.md` (Scheduled-prompts config section) document the new `priority` field, the default-`high` behaviour, and the three routines; the maintenance-routines skill is referenced from the relevant skill docs listing.
6. **Testing criterion.** Skill tests (`pytest` under `skill/maintenance-routines/tests/`) cover reconcile/idempotence/preservation/dry-run; herdr unit tests (`vitest`) cover the new parse/validation and dispatch priority; full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No changes to the interactive dispatch path or to the other downtime tiers' mapping tables** (`request-priority.ts` stays fixed); only the scheduled-prompt entry schema, its dispatch call, and the skill/template change.
- The requested **default is `high`** for scheduled prompts (operator decision Q1): an entry that wants lower priority must set the field explicitly (`low`/`medium`). This is a deliberate change from the current downtime default (`medium`) for scheduled prompts only.
- No code-behaviour changes to `wl init` — only the **contents** of `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the provisioning path and create-if-absent semantics stay as-is).
- The skill must be safe to run from any project root (`wl`-independent — it reads/writes only `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, atomic tmp+rename, matching herdr's `saveScheduledPrompts` pattern).

## Existing state

- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (and the live `/.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`) currently carry only `/skill:refactor` (3-day interval, no time) and `/skill:standup` (daily `time: "06:05"`); no `/skill:test`; no priority field anywhere.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — schema (`id|prompt|intervalDays|lastTriggeredAt|time?`), fail-closed parse, due-check, atomic persist; **no priority support**.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchScheduledPrompt` calls `spawnAgentPane(prompt.prompt, { model, cwd, paneName, anchorId })` with **no priority** → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions({ priority: undefined })` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority(undefined)` → `medium` (docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md, "Scheduled prompts have no work item and get the downtime default (medium)").
- `src/commands/init.ts` — `ensureScheduledPromptsInstalled` copies the template create-if-absent; unchanged in behaviour.
- Skills precedent: `skill/heartbeat/` and `skill/pane-triage/` (SKILL.md + scripts + tests, tracked in ContextHub, deployed to `~/.pi/agent/skills/<name>`); shared helpers in `skill/shared/`.

## Desired change

1. **New skill** `skill/maintenance-routines/`: `SKILL.md` (spec: required-routines table, invocation, admission of a bootstrap `/skill:maintenance-routines` schedule), `scripts/maintenance_routines.py` (reconcile + `--dry-run`; atomic writes; preserves `lastTriggeredAt` and foreign entries), `tests/` (unit tests).
2. **Herdr priority support**: extend `ScheduledPrompt` + `parseScheduledPrompt` with optional `priority` (default `high`); thread it from `dispatchScheduledPrompt` → `spawnAgentPane({ priority })` → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`. `mapDowntimeRequestPriority` already maps `high`→`high`.
3. **Template**: update `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` to the three routines (daily, timed, `priority: "high"`).
4. **Docs**: `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CONFIG.md`; skill listed alongside heartbeat/pane-triage where appropriate.
5. **Tests**: pytest for the skill reconciler; vitest for parse/validation + dispatch threading in herdr.

## Key Files

- `skill/maintenance-routines/SKILL.md` — new skill spec (required-routines table, usage, dry-run).
- `skill/maintenance-routines/scripts/maintenance_routines.py` — new reconciler CLI (`--dry-run`, atomic write, preserves state).
- `skill/maintenance-routines/tests/test_maintenance_routines.py` — new unit tests (reconcile, idempotence, preservation, malformed config, dry-run).
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — add optional `priority` (`low|medium|high|critical`, default `high`), validation in `parseScheduledPrompt`.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.test.ts` — new parse/default/validation cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchScheduledPrompt` passes `prompt.priority` to `spawnAgentPane`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (or the scheduled-prompts tier test) — dispatch threads `priority: 'high'` into the spawn opts/env.
- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` — updated to the three required routines.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CONFIG.md` — document the new field/default and the routines.
- `tests/skill/maintenance-routines/` — integration-style tests for the skill (repo test-suite convention, cf. `tests/skill/heartbeat/`).

## Related work

- **WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX** (completed) — herdr downtime dispatcher: scheduled prompts (best-effort frequency) config — the mechanism the skill maintains.
- **WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH / WL-0MVF3Q3VL000UNCN** (completed) — request priority (`X-Priority`) mapping tables and `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` env threading — the priority plumbing we reuse.
- **WL-0MTF5UAJ4000LLZ9** (completed) — removal of scheduled-prompts console output (no-op here).
- **WL-0MUKYERLZ006ELL5** (completed) — non-terminal cooldown for dispatched panes (context for scheduled dispatch behaviour).
- **WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B** (completed) — periodic request scheduling to the pi worklog plugin; the scheduled-prompts feature parent.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B** – Add periodic request scheduling to pi worklog plugin (completed)
- **WL-0MTMN7W63001FCQR** – Scheduled prompts: add time-of-day dispatch (time window) to scheduled-prompts tier (completed)
- **WL-0MKRPG64S04PL1A6** – wl doctor (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: convey, create, creates, currently, daily (+26 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: create, creates, daily, default, dispatched (+25 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: convey, create, creates, currently, default (+23 more)
- Skill-authoring precedents: `skill/heartbeat/`, `skill/pane-triage/` (SKILL.md + scripts + tests, deployed to `~/.pi/agent/skills`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — default-`high` changes politeness of ALL scheduled prompts** (including custom future entries). Accepted by operator (Q1: "default high"); any entry can opt down via an explicit `low`/`medium` field. Mitigation: document prominently.
- **Risk — parse strictness.** An invalid `priority` value rejects the whole entry (consistent with existing `time` handling) — a config typo could silently disable a routine. Mitigation: the skill always writes a valid value; tests cover the failure path.

# Herdr downtime dispatch: claim local capacity via proxy reservation (never send-then-hope)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher polls `/llama/local/status` and launches panes into what it believes is free capacity. Two defects remain even after `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` (prefill-gate pacing) ships:

1. **Poll-and-send is racy.** With the prefill gate serialised (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`), new starts are a single ticket. Two herdr instances polling in the same 10 s tick can both be admitted and launch; the second queues behind the first's prefill and, on the current proxy, times out and goes remote (measured on the proxy side: queue depth reached 7 in-window while `available_slots` still reported 2 with the gate saturated; 261 requests fell back after queueing, 215 after the full 120 s). An idle window can be *observed* by N instances but only *owned* by one.
2. **The sent-work model is wrong for mid-session pressure.** Even with correct pane pacing, pane turns are continuous (29 sessions, median 30 requests/session on 2026-10-21); those turns cannot be gated by idle windows at all. The dispatcher (and the agents it spawns) must be able to claim capacity *per request* and defer when refused.

The proxy is adding an atomic reservation handshake — `POST /llama/local/reserve` returning a gate ticket, or a `429 {reason, retry_after_s}` refusal — plus `X-Local-Preference: local-only` and `X-Local-Route`/`X-Local-Fallback-Reason` response headers (llm-manager `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL`). This item consumes that handshake so the dispatcher never launches work it cannot start.

## Goal / users

- As the downtime dispatcher, I want to launch exactly **one pane per idle window** (operator requirement, asserted in the comment on `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`): I ask the proxy for a ticket, launch only with a ticket, and defer with `retry_after` when refused — never poll-then-hope.
- As an agent session spawned by herdr, I want per-turn capacity claims so my turns either get a ticket (local) or an immediate, honest refusal to fall back (remote) — never a silent 120 s proxy-side wait.

## Desired change

1. **Reservation client:** on each dispatch decision, call `POST /llama/local/reserve` (reusing the existing single-flight status poll cadence; no new polling) with the pane's expected token size, priority and cache state.
   - Ticket granted → launch with `X-Local-Reservation` on the first request; treat the ticket as the pane's entry to the gate.
   - Refused (`429`) → defer with `retry_after`, record decision reason (`reserved-fallback` / `prefill-gate` / `queue-full`…).
   - Endpoint absent / failure → fail-open fall back to the `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` polling behaviour (never a hard failure against an older proxy).
2. **One-per-idle-window assertion:** after a successful launch, no second pane is launched until a fresh status tick shows `local_prefills_in_flight < local_max_concurrent_prefills` **and** the reservation was granted for that specific launch. Test the two-instances-same-tick race.
3. **Per-turn claims for agent sessions:** the herdr agent runner passes `X-Local-Preference: local-only` for work the operator marks local-first and `remote-ok` for background work; turns then receive the proxy's honest refusal instead of a silent fallback, and the runner records `X-Local-Route`/`X-Local-Fallback-Reason` from responses into the decision log.
4. **Decision-log evidence:** each dispatch/defer records ticket state, `admit`, `projected_wait_s`, `retry_after_s`, and the response route headers.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — reserve client:** when the proxy serves the reserve endpoint (fixture), a dispatch first receives a ticket and only then launches with the reservation header; a refused ticket defers with `retry_after` and is recorded (`downtime-worker.mock.test.ts`-style mocked fetch, following the existing fixture pattern).
2. **AC2 — failure mode backcompat:** endpoint absent/500/timeout → exactly today's polling behaviour, no crash, no stuck pane (tests for each).
3. **AC3 — one-per-idle-window:** two instances observing the same idle window produce at most one launch; the second defers with the refusal evidence (test modelling the same-tick race).
4. **AC4 — per-turn preference:** the runner sends `X-Local-Preference` per configured policy, parses `X-Local-Route`/`X-Local-Fallback-Reason`, and records both in the decision log (tests).
5. **AC5 — docs:** `packages/herdr/README.md` and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` document the reservation handshake, the one-per-idle-window rule, and the preference policy knob.
6. **AC6 — suite:** full project test suite passes via the test skill.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing single-flight status poll; the reservation call may piggyback on the same request cadence (no new polling loops).
- Fail-open: an older proxy is fully supported — absent fields/endpoint never block dispatch.
- Pacing only reduces concurrency; never raise the free-slot budget, never bypass fail-closed per-slot handling (`WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW`).
- Keep it surgical: this item extends `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`'s pacing with the atomic claim; it does not rewrite the dispatcher.

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — reserve call, ticket header, deferral on refusal.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.parse.test.ts` / `.idle.test.ts` / `.test.ts` / `.fixtures.ts` — reserve + race tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/` agent-runner request path — `X-Local-Preference`, route-header parsing, decision log.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

## Related work

- **Depends on:** llm-manager `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` (proxy reservation endpoint + headers); adopts the contract it ACs.
- **Extends:** `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` (prefill-gate pacing — poll-based); its comment asserts the one-per-idle-window requirement.
- **Siblings:** `WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P` (per-slot capacity, completed/in_review), `WL-0MVHSZR9C0012NQY` (idle-age signal), `WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW` (fail-closed per-slot availability).
- **Proxy-side quad:** `LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV` (occupancy-aware guard, prerequisite), `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` (reservation, this item's dependency), `LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R` (queue sweep after reservations).

## Risks

- **Reservation latency:** an extra round trip per dispatch. Mitigation: piggyback on the status poll cadence and measure; the ticket TTL covers the launch.
- **Over-deferral:** a pessimistic proxy refusal could starve panes. Mitigation: refusals only on calibrated verdicts (proxy fail-open) and the client-side fail-open path.
- **Contract drift:** the proxy contract is new; version the request (additive fields) and keep the fail-open parsing strict-but-tolerant.

## Goal

As an operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`, I want the CPU / memory / I/O stall pressure metrics to report real values, so the diagnosis is based on the kernel's own pressure-stall signal instead of silently losing three of its twelve metrics.

## Problem

`scripts/metrics.py::_read_proc_pressure()` always returns `None` on Linux, so `cpu_pressure`, `memory_pressure` and `io_pressure` are permanently rendered as:

```
| cpu_pressure    | n/a | 🟡 | P1 | warning |
```

with the description "unavailable (non-Linux or kernel missing pressure stall info)", even though PSI is present and readable.

## Evidence (verified 2026-10-21, 16-core Ubuntu host)

```
$ cat /proc/pressure/cpu
some avg10=11.58 avg60=7.68 avg300=11.33 total=71756189671
full avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=0

$ cat /proc/pressure/memory
some avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=54872967

$ cat /proc/pressure/io
some avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=242601913
```

So genuine CPU `some` pressure was ~11.6 percent (moderate contention, consistent with load 11.92 on 16 cores) and would have been visible. Instead the run reported all three as n/a.

## Root cause

```python
for line in lines:
    if line.startswith("avg"):            # <-- never true
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) >= 4:
            return float(parts[1])
return None
```

PSI lines are prefixed `some ` or `full `, never `avg`. The tokens are `avg10=<v>`, `avg60=<v>`, `avg300=<v>` — not space-separated bare numbers — so even a corrected prefix match would index the wrong field and would need `split("=")`.

## Suggested fix

```python
def _read_proc_pressure(key: str, which: str = "some") -> float | None:
    """Return avg10 stall percentage for /proc/pressure/<key>."""
    lines = _read_file_lines(f"/proc/pressure/{key}")
    if lines is None:
        return None
    for line in lines:
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) >= 2 and parts[0] == which:
            for token in parts[1:]:
                if token.startswith("avg10="):
                    try:
                        return float(token.split("=", 1)[1])
                    except ValueError:
                        return None
    return None
```

Semantics to decide explicitly:

- `/proc/pressure/cpu` exposes only a `some` line. `/proc/pressure/memory` and `/proc/pressure/io` expose both `some` and `full`.
- Recommended: use `some` for `cpu_pressure` (any task stalled on CPU) and `full` for `memory_pressure` / `io_pressure` (all tasks stalled — the severe, actionable signal). Whatever is chosen must be documented in `SKILL.md` and in the metric `description`.
- The classification config key for `memory_pressure` is currently wired to the `memory_usage` thresholds (`pressure_specs` tuple `("memory", "memory_pressure", "memory_usage", ...)`). Once PSI parses, decide whether memory *pressure* stall percent should share the 80/95 *usage* thresholds or get its own `memory_pressure` block in `config.yaml` / `config.py::_DEFAULTS`. Note `config.yaml` has no `memory_pressure` section despite the SKILL.md metric table listing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `_read_proc_pressure` parses real `/proc/pressure/*` content and returns the `avg10` stall percentage for the selected `some`/`full` line; a unit test feeds verbatim `/proc/pressure` sample content for cpu (some only) and memory/io (some + full) and asserts the expected values.
- AC2: A unit test covers the failure modes: file missing -> `None`; file present but unparsable -> `None`; requested `full` line absent -> documented fallback behaviour.
- AC3: `scripts/evaluate.py` on a Linux host with PSI enabled renders numeric `cpu_pressure` / `memory_pressure` / `io_pressure` values (no `n/a`), verified by an actual run pasted into a comment on this item.
- AC4: The `some` vs `full` choice per metric is documented in `SKILL.md` and reflected in each metric's `description`.
- AC5: The threshold wiring for `memory_pressure` is either explicitly mapped to `memory_usage` (with a code comment and SKILL.md note justifying it) or given its own `memory_pressure` config block in `config.yaml` and `config.py::_DEFAULTS`.
- AC6: Degradation on non-Linux / PSI-less kernels still yields `None` and the existing "unavailable" message — unchanged, no crash.
- AC7: Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

## Key files

- `scripts/metrics.py` — `_read_proc_pressure()` (~line 105), `pressure_specs` loop (~line 352)
- `scripts/config.py` — `_DEFAULTS` (add `memory_pressure` block if AC5 chooses that route)
- `config.yaml` — thresholds / documentation
- `SKILL.md` — metric table and `some`/`full` semantics
- `tests/` — new PSI parser unit tests

## Notes

- The skill currently lives only at `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/` (not tracked in this repo). Fixing it here means either promoting the skill into `skill/machine-hygiene/` alongside `skill/pane-triage/` (this repo's canonical home for global agent-framework skills) or patching the global copy by hand. Worth deciding as part of this item.
- Found alongside two already-filed machine-hygiene defects: WL-0MVI8YM07002Z9VY (threshold miscalibration) and WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ (duplicate proposed actions). All three were surfaced by the same run; this one is the loss-of-signal defect.
